findings.title: rows.slice(1, limit + 1) drops the first (newest) row
findings.explanation: slice(1, ...) skips index 0, so every page loses its first invoice and returns only `limit - 1` items when more exist. Those invoices are never shown to the client, since the next page starts from `id < last`. Use rows.slice(0, limit) to keep the first `limit` rows and drop only the extra lookahead row.

findings.title: next_before can be computed from the wrong row / crash on empty page
findings.explanation: With the slice bug, a request with limit = 1 and 2 rows returns an empty page (slice(1,2) gives one row, but with limit = 1 and exactly 2 rows hasMore is true and page has 1 row, so fine; however if limit = 0 or rows is shortened, page can be empty and page[page.length - 1].id throws a TypeError). Fix the slice first, and make sure limit is validated to be >= 1 so page is never empty when hasMore is true.

findings.title: limit validation and upper bound not visible
findings.explanation: Now that limit + 1 is sent to the query, an unvalidated or very large `limit` (NaN, negative, 0, or huge) has an even bigger effect (e.g. NaN + 1 is NaN, which breaks the SQL parameter). Confirm that `limit` is parsed as an integer and clamped to a sensible range (e.g. 1..100) before use, and that the cap applies to the user-requested value, not to limit + 1.

findings.title: No tests for pagination boundary cases
findings.explanation: This bug class (off-by-one at page boundaries) is easy to regress and the slice bug above would have been caught by a test. Add tests for: fewer than limit rows, exactly limit rows (next_before null), limit + 1 rows (next_before set to the last returned id), and walking all pages to verify no invoice is skipped or duplicated.

findings.title: Clarify naming of the lookahead row
findings.explanation: Consider a short comment explaining that one extra row is fetched purely to detect another page, and perhaps name the constant (e.g. `const fetchLimit = limit + 1`) so the intent is clear to later readers.

prompt:
Review this pull request.

## Fix next_before when the last page is exactly full

When the last page had exactly `limit` invoices, `next_before` was still set, so the web app made one extra request that came back empty. This fetches `limit + 1` rows to know whether another page exists.

## Diff

```diff
diff --git a/src/routes/invoices.ts b/src/routes/invoices.ts
index b9edb19..8e99e4e 100644
--- a/src/routes/invoices.ts
+++ b/src/routes/invoices.ts
@@ -19,11 +19,13 @@ invoicesRouter.get('/', async (req, res) => {
       WHERE org_id = $1 AND ($2::bigint IS NULL OR id < $2)
       ORDER BY id DESC
       LIMIT $3`,
-    [req.user.orgId, before ?? null, limit],
+    [req.user.orgId, before ?? null, limit + 1],
   )
+  const hasMore = rows.length > limit
+  const page = rows.slice(1, limit + 1)
   res.json({
-    invoices: rows.map(serializeInvoice),
-    next_before: rows.length === limit ? rows[rows.length - 1].id : null,
+    invoices: page.map(serializeInvoice),
+    next_before: hasMore ? page[page.length - 1].id : null,
   })
 })
```
